name: GZip & Deflate
description: Compress and decompress gzip, zlib and raw deflate data.

results.outputHint: The result can be copied directly.

hints.input: For compression the input is the original content; for decompression it is the compressed stream, so set the input encoding to the form it is actually stored in.
hints.format: gzip, zlib and raw deflate are three different containers; mixing them up makes decompression fail.
hints.output: The ratio is output bytes over input bytes; after decompression it shows how large the payload expands.

faq.q: What is the difference between gzip and deflate?
faq.a: gzip carries a file header and a CRC checksum, zlib (the deflate container) carries a two-byte header and an Adler-32 checksum, and raw deflate has no wrapper at all.
Usually the container format is wrong: feeding gzip data to the raw deflate reader fails. Also make sure the input encoding matches how the data is actually stored.
